claims.text: In Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7, phase stability after high-temperature BCC processing is governed by a balance between composition-driven thermodynamic instability and kinetic limitations from atomic mobility.
Al promotes local chemical ordering in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Al-induced local chemical ordering lowers the alloy's free energy and supplies the thermodynamic driving force for transformation.
Atomic diffusion limits the rate at which ordering develops.
The extent of transformation can be approximated as being governed by the product of local ordering energy and atomic mobility.
The relevant structural mediator is an Al-mediated, ordered B2-like secondary phase within the BCC matrix.
Longer isothermal holds below the BCC stability region will increase the ordered-phase fraction.
Slower cooling through the sub-transition regime will increase the ordered-phase fraction.
Rapid quenching will preserve more of the metastable high-temperature BCC structure.
Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 can be established initially as a high-temperature BCC phase.
A temperature range of approximately 650–750°C lies near but below the BCC stability region for this composition.
Within the proposed 650–750°C window, ordering is thermodynamically favored while diffusion remains moderately limited.
Thermodynamic phase stability and transformation behavior can vary with composition and temperature.
The controlled comparison keeps composition and initial processing constant while varying hold duration and cooling rate.
Failure of longer holds or slower cooling to produce a systematic measurable increase in ordered-phase fraction relative to rapid quenching would falsify the proposed kinetic-evolution hypothesis.
